plan_area_inventory.title: Canonical dev-environment profile schema and persistence (operator-seeded, agent-maintained) with names-only secret refs
Deterministic detection of local vs docker-host-local vs remote automation targets; compose with US-0064 / US-0086
Execute-phase dev relaunch after implementation changes (bounded triggers; not release-only startup)
Docker / docker compose rebuild-and-up recipes with fail-closed diagnostics when profile or stack unresolved
Operator-visible connection summary after relaunch (URL, port, health, service/container id; no secret values)
Scratchpad-gated automation profile default-off; manual daily work unchanged when disabled
Compose with US-0065 runtime autopilot, US-0086 routing, US-0085 .env exclusion, DEV_SERVER_* scratchpad keys
Phase commands, runbook, optional stdlib helper, contract tests, and template parity

topic_coverage.quoted_user_text: During development the AI should automatically rebuild and restart the running app after code changes — for example rebuild Docker containers — and show me connection parameters, instead of only validating at QA or release.

This is dev-loop inside the detected developer environment: when I code on the Docker host itself I use local shell and docker commands, not remote SSH; optional Docker/SSH targets from existing remote config when automation is enabled.

Build on existing its-magic contracts: Python stdlib helpers, scratchpad keys like DEV_SERVER_COMMAND, .cursor/remote.json, release-targets.json, and stack-aware startup from US-0065 — not a parallel ad-hoc connection string layer.

The agent should detect where development runs, persist a dev-environment profile the operator can seed once with parameters, then reuse automatically; default-off scratchpad gate like AUTO_REMOTE_AUTOMATION_PROFILE so manual daily work stays unchanged.
After relaunch, present operator-ready connection info in chat or handoff output: URL or host:port, health check path, service or container id — secrets as env-var names only, never values.
Same rules as US-0085: agents must not read .env; persisted dev profile stores env reference names only; no secret literals in git-tracked JSON or handoffs.

Bounded rebuild and restart with fail-closed reason codes, idempotent profile updates, and explicit manual override; avoid infinite watch loops in the first delivery unless architecture proves a safe bounded trigger.

Single story if sprint sizing allows; clearly distinct from US-0065 phase startup, US-0086 test routing, and US-0067 release Run/Connect hints; trigger at minimum after execute tasks with optional explicit refresh command.
